items.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
items.snippet: WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account. The WordPress plugins team has independently detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now
items.summary: Six backdoored plugins from WP Connect were removed by WordPress before malicious updates went live, preventing arbitrary code execution. Check your WordPress site for affected plugins and remove them immediately.

When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (`orig`). Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTM…

livewire-powergrid: SQL injection via sortDirection in naturalSort queries
items.snippet: The public Livewire property `sortDirection` is interpolated verbatim into a raw SQL `ORDER BY` clause and is not restricted to `asc`/`desc`, allowing arbitrary SQL injection through `POST /livewire/update`. Data flow - Source — `src/Concerns/Sorting.php`: `public string $sortDirection;` is a Livewire-bound property with no whitelist/validation (it is only assigned and flipped by `reverseSort()`)…
items.summary: Livewire Powergrid is vulnerable to SQL injection via the sortDirection property in naturalSort queries, affecting Laravel developers using livewire-powergrid. Upgrade power-components/livewire-powergrid to 6.10.4 or later.
